chapter.title: Rexx in .NET Programs
chapter.para: A .NET program runs Rexx code through the Rexx.Net package: to let its users script it, to keep rules in Rexx, or to reuse Rexx code. These recipes are in C#; VB.NET and PowerShell use the same types.

section.title: Scripting an Application
section.para: You want to let Rexx scripts drive your application's objects.

example.title: Scripting an Application

section.para: How it works. A .NET object given to Rexx (here through .local) is a NetObject there, used with Rexx messages: the script calls the application's own methods and properties. A routine compiled once (Compile) is called many times, cheaply, and its result converted (Call<decimal>): rules that users can change without rebuilding the application. Rexx's arithmetic is decimal, so 120 × 0.9 is exactly 108.0. (FormattableString.Invariant writes it with a point on every machine; C#'s $"..." alone uses the machine's culture.)
See also Reference, .NET Using ooRexx: the Rexx.Net API, Both Ways in One Process.

section.title: Using a Rexx Class from C#
section.para: You want to use a class written in Rexx from C#.

example.title: Using a Rexx Class from C#

section.para: How it works. LoadPackage loads Rexx source (or a file) as a package, and FindClass gives its class. Its objects are RexxObjects: through dynamic, a member is a Rexx message (a.deposit(5) sends DEPOSIT), and a result converts to the C# type it is used as; Send and Send<T> do the same without dynamic.
See also Reference, .NET Using ooRexx: the Rexx.Net API, RexxObject Class.

section.title: Taking Rexx's Output
section.para: You want Rexx's SAY in your application (a log, a text box), and its PULL from it.

example.title: Taking Rexx's Output

section.para: How it works. Output, Error and Input take any TextWriter and TextReader, at any time; null gives the process's own streams back. A Windows Forms application writes to a text box with a small TextWriter of its own.
See also Reference, The Application's Environment, Standard Streams.

section.title: Commands for Your Application
section.para: You want Rexx scripts that send commands to your application, as macros do.

example.title: Commands for Your Application
example.screen: REXXout>lines: 2 REXXout>rc: 1 first line / second line

section.para: How it works. A command environment is a C# function that gets each command (RexxCommand), with the caller's variables (cmd["LINES"] = ... sets one), and returns RC. With InitialAddress, a plain string clause is a command to the application, as in an editor's macros. RexxCommandException raises Rexx's ERROR condition, with its RC; not trapped, the script goes on with RC set.
See also Reference, The Application's Environment, ADDRESS Environments.

section.title: VB.NET and PowerShell
section.para: You want to run Rexx from VB.NET, or from PowerShell.

How it works. VB.NET uses the same types: with Option Strict Off, a Rexx object typed Object is late-bound as C#'s dynamic, and its results convert by type (Dim n As Integer = acct.Balance). A class's New is [New] in VB. The project's samples/vbnet/tour is samples/csharp/tour written again in VB.NET, topic by topic.
PowerShell 7.4 or later loads the assembly with Add-Type -Path Rexx.Net.dll, and then:
A Rexx string is a RexxString: .ToString() gives PowerShell a string. Windows PowerShell 5.1 runs on .NET Framework, and cannot load the bridge. The sample is samples/powershell/hello.ps1.
See also Reference, Both Ways in One Process, The NuGet Package.
